8.description: Saskatoon Police Service updated on community events like Red Dress Day, the Missing Person's Gallery, and the annual Pride BBQ, plus the citizen police perception survey.

chips.text: Initiatives support families of murdered and missing Indigenous women.
Chief promised to share citizen police perception survey results with the board.

18.description: Saskatoon Police reported on 2024 incidents where drivers fled from peace officers, noting an increase in no-pursuit evasions and consistent pursuit numbers, with no serious injuries.

chips.text: Chief McBride attributed reduced air support interventions to pilot and mechanical issues.

19.description: Saskatoon Police Service reported a 26% decrease in use of force incidents in 2025, occurring in only 0.17% of calls. This annual report promotes transparency and accountability.

chips.text: Commissioner Block noted the low use of force rate addresses common public misconceptions.
The report covers Saskatoon's estimated population of 316,342 residents.

20.description: Saskatoon Police Service finds it difficult to accurately track instances where PACT teams are needed but unavailable due to subjective call classification and manual data extraction challenges.

chips.text: Commissioner Jeffries pressed for tracking unmet PACT demand, suggesting statistical analysis.
Staff highlighted difficulty tracking PACT availability; council sought solutions.
Unmet PACT team availability for mental health crises can lead to more police intervention.
Administration will report further on PACT statistics and a jurisdictional analysis.
